name: Prior Art First Look — Retrieval Engine

parameters.content:
## Seed and expand — do not query once

The Build Query Plan node multiplies one disclosure into many CQL variants (concept x synonym, plus CPC-scoped variants). Recall is governed by vocabulary match, not data coverage: "stepped" and "gradient" describe the same structure but return completely different result sets.

Zero results is a signal to broaden, never an answer — see the Seeds Found? branch.

## Examiner citations are the strongest leg

EPO OPS biblio carries references-cited with examiner relevance categories (X / Y / A). This converts one lucky keyword hit into an examiner-validated art set — art that no keyword query in this run returned.

This stage is mandatory, not optional.

## The fabrication guardrail

Validate And Assemble Report builds an allow-list of every identifier that actually came back from an API, then drops anything not on it and LOGS the drop. Silent filtering is not acceptable — a fabrication attempt is signal.

Every output carries its own coverage statement, known-gap list and scope limitation.

parameters.sqlQuery:
WITH cov AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS n
  FROM `REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_GCP_PROJECT_ID.prior_art.us_claims_by_cpc`
  WHERE cpc_prefix = @cpcPrefix
),
hits AS (
  SELECT publication_number, country_code, publication_date, title
  FROM `REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_GCP_PROJECT_ID.prior_art.us_claims_by_cpc`
  WHERE cpc_prefix = @cpcPrefix
    AND REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(claims_text), @conceptPattern)
    AND REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(claims_text), @synonymPattern)
    AND (@dateBefore = '' OR publication_date < CAST(@dateBefore AS INT64))
  ORDER BY publication_date DESC
  LIMIT 25
)
SELECT 'hit' AS row_type, h.publication_number, h.country_code, h.publication_date, h.title, (SELECT n FROM cov) AS subset_docs
FROM hits AS h
UNION ALL
SELECT 'coverage', NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, (SELECT n FROM cov)

parameters.content:
## BigQuery — US claims full text, from a materialised subset

Searches `prior_art.us_claims_by_cpc`, a clustered table built once per CPC area by the **BigQuery Prior-Art Subset Builder** workflow. C25B built 2026-08-28: **23,368 US documents**, 1950-01-10 to 2026-04-21.

**Why a subset.** Querying `patents-public-data` directly measured **~157 GB per run** — about six runs inside BigQuery's 1 TiB monthly free tier. The subset pays that scan once per art area and makes every later search small enough that `maximumBytesBilled` at 5 GB is a real ceiling rather than a formality.

**Do not use the node's `dryRun` option as a cost guard.** Tested 2026-08-28: with `dryRun: true` set, the node still executed and billed the query. `maximumBytesBilled` is the guard here — BigQuery refuses an over-ceiling job without charge — though that behaviour has not itself been independently verified.

The query returns a coverage row so a genuine zero-hit result can be told apart from a CPC area with no subset built. Run the Subset Builder for A61K, C12N or any other area you work in.

## Auto-build on a cache miss — PROOF OF CONCEPT

If a search names a CPC subclass with no subset, this branch starts the **BigQuery Prior-Art Subset Builder** for that subclass and returns immediately.

**It does not wait.** A build is a one-time ~157 GB scan taking minutes; the MCP caller times out at 60 seconds. The current run still reports that US claims text was not searched, and tells the user to re-run.

### Know what this spends

- Each auto-build is **~157 GB**. BigQuery's free tier is 1 TiB/month, so roughly **six builds** before the meter starts.
- **Any caller can trigger one.** The MCP trigger ships unauthenticated, so anyone with the Production URL can spend your BigQuery bytes by searching an unbuilt area. Set Bearer auth if that matters.
- **There is no in-flight lock.** Re-running the same search before the build finishes fires a second build for the same prefix. Two calls, ~314 GB. Wait for the first to finish.

The Subset Builder refuses any prefix that is not a 4-character CPC subclass — an empty prefix makes `STARTS_WITH(cp.code, '')` true for every row and would insert the entire US corpus.
